scope: Theorem 3.2 (Compressed consistency reduction) of the manuscript “Unconditional time lower bounds for Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence” (preprints/Unconditional-time-lower-bounds-for-Weisfeiler-Leman-equivalence-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 133 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5d58d0f7cee1b9ed), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For fixed r and fixed description shape, an instance as above determines two equally large simple uncolored connected graphs G0, G1, of diameter at most two and order Or,shape(m6 ), such that Duplicator wins the K-pair bijective game on G0, G1 if and only if the instance has individual-edge arc consistency. The construction uses the bounded scalar-form data together with the one-coordinate tables, and enumerates Or,shape(m2) blocks without enumerating all full addresses. An arbitrary equal number of additional vertices can be added to the two graphs while preserving the equivalence, connectedness, and diameter bound.
